thread:
mike_sales: Quick sync - DesktopHealth wants to run a 2-week Private deployment POC next week. Net/Security wants to know if we can: preserve client IP headers for their analytics, support mTLS to our connector, and not require opening wide CIDR ranges. Also asking about any pricing delta for static egress IPs.

elaine_se: Short answer: yes to mTLS, and yes to static egress, but IP preservation depends on topology. If they need original client IP in an HTTP header (X-Forwarded-For) we can add that on the connector side as a header (app-level), which is easiest. If they need L3/L4 source preservation we need peering/direct routing.

mike_sales: They said their compliance team won't accept app-level headers for auditing, they need the source preserved at L3 so their IDS sees the origin.

tom_neteng: Understood. Patterns we support: 1) PrivateLink/interface endpoint (recommended for locked-down VPCs) -> connector sits in their VPC, traffic is from connector ENI so L3 IP changed. 2) VPC Peering or Transit Gateway -> we can route directly and preserve client source IPs, but requires symmetric routing and firewall rules. 3) GRE/DMVPN -> possible but adds ops complexity. For fastest POC: use PrivateLink first and capture functional tests; if L3 preservation is mandatory, follow up with peering/TGW.

kevin_platform: Pricing for static egress: managed static IPs are an add-on on top of Private deployment. Options:
- Managed EIP pool (ours) attached to NAT gateway: one-time setup fee + monthly per-EIP charge + small per-GB surcharge.
- Customer-owned EIPs (BYOIP): cheaper monthly, but requires their procurement.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved) bundles can include static IPs in contract at discounted rate.

infra-bot: note: infra maintenance window 2025-05-28 02:00-04:00 UTC may impact provisioning if requested during that window.

elaine_se: For the firewall ACLs, here's a minimal list they can hand to their team. Confirm exact addresses with infra before they apply.
```
- Outbound TCP 443 to: 34.212.11.77, 34.212.11.78 (Redwood test ENIs)
- Outbound TCP 8443 to: 34.212.11.79 (optional management plane)
- DNS UDP/TCP 53 to their resolver or allowed resolver IP
- NTP UDP 123 (recommended)
- Allow return ephemeral ports 1024-65535 if using NAT
- Allow ICMP type 3,4 for PMTU discovery
```

mike_sales: They use a Palo Alto and prefer whitelisting by FQDN if possible. Can we provide FQDNs?

tom_neteng: PrivateLink supports private DNS so they can resolve service.<company>.privatelink.redwood.ai -> map to ENIs internally. For firewall appliances that only support FQDN allowlist for egress, we can provide customer-facing FQDNs but DNS-based allowlisting is weaker. If they insist on IPs, we'll provide EIP list for the POC.

elaine_se: MTU note: some SD-WAN boxes use 1350-1400. Recommend testing MTU and set MSS clamp on their firewall for TCP to avoid TLS fragmentation. Quick test: `ping -M do -s 1372 <peer-ip>` (adjust for headers).

kevin_platform: Security questionnaire rapid answers:
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployment; HSM-backed keys available under enterprise addendum.
- Data residency: Private deploy keeps model inference inside their VPC; we can disable payload logging.
- Audit logs: request-level metadata (no PII) can be exported to S3/CloudWatch.
- SOC2: available upon NDA/enterprise pack.

mike_sales: They also want a simple curl test they can run to validate TLS and headers.

elaine_se: Share this snippet for mTLS health check (they'll need client cert/key we provide for test):

```bash
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key -v https://internal-catalog.privatelink.redwood.ai:443/health
```

For non-mTLS test: `curl -v https://internal-catalog.privatelink.redwood.ai:443/health`

tom_neteng: If they want L3 preservation via peering, firewall team needs to allow these networks and ensure return path to our ASN. Minimal routing checklist:
- Create peering between their VPC (10.20.0.0/16) and our service VPC (10.30.0.0/16) OR attach to TGW
- Add route for our service subnets -> point to peering/TGW
- Ensure security groups allow ingress from their CIDR to connector ports (443, 8443)
- Natting: disable connector NAT if preserving src IPs; verify SNAT rules in their appliance

kevin_platform: Ops note: IP-preserve peering requires a short design review (1-2 business days) and a ticket to infra to provision routes and security groups. POC can still start with PrivateLink while design is happening.

mike_sales: Timeline: customer wants a test by Tuesday. Can we get test EIPs + certs by Monday EOD?

tom_neteng: I'll queue a request for test ENIs/EIPs and ping infra; aim for Monday EOD. Need primary contact from DesktopHealth netops (name + sshable ip for troubleshooting).

mike_sales: contact is netops lead 'carla.netops@desktophealth.com' - I'll loop her in once we have the EIPs.

elaine_se: I'll prepare a trimmed checklist and curl scripts to hand to Carla.

kevin_platform: I'll draft the pricing delta and include a one-line about discounts if they commit to 12-month reserved capacity.

mike_sales: Perfect. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
